dataset.title: Targeting Senescent Stem-Like Subpopulations in Philadelphia Chromosome-Like Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

findings.message: The search identified an unusually small fraction of the MS2 spectra. Treat absence of a protein in this dataset as weak evidence. Producer's note: 119179/828121 = 14.39% of MS2 identified (S3)

no SDRF says which sample is in which channel (no curated design and no deposited SDRF); PXReprise's default design makes each file its own plex and each channel that shows a sample its own sample (marked empty, holding none: 134C in 26 file(s), 135N in 26 file(s)); the reporter values compare nothing until a design is curated (QuantProject 079)

No SDRF was found for this dataset, so each channel's sample is the sample its search's TmtDesign.txt names (its `Sample Name`), with nothing else known about it. There is no sample metadata: treat every sample as unannotated.

Some modifications on peptides shared between proteins were not written to ptm_sites for one or more of those proteins, because the peptide could not be located in that protein's sequence and the producer's residue spans cannot be paired with its accessions. Of the (PSM, protein) pairs affected: 261 named a protein that does not contain the stored peptide -- typically a PSM ambiguous between peptide sequences (level 4 or 5), where this protein carries a different candidate than the first, which is the one stored. Sites on the other proteins of the same PSMs are written. Counts are in bundle.json under protein_databases.

1 modification(s) could not be mapped to a UNIMOD accession or a mass, and are carried in ProForma as [Info:...] tags: UniProt:5-glutamyl histamine on Q. Their ptm_sites rows exist and carry modification_name, with modification null, so a query by name finds them and a query by UNIMOD accession will not.

1 of the 26 files were searched as acquired, not calibrated (their names in the search carry no `-calib`): `Tio2_3rd_2`. Their reporter values are the same kind of number; their identifications rest on uncalibrated precursor masses (QuantProject 066, rule 3).

52 channel(s) of the search's TmtDesign.txt are not study samples: `Sample Type` empty: `PXD053611:Fe_1st_1_2:TMT134C`, `PXD053611:Fe_1st_1_2:TMT135N`, `PXD053611:Fe_1st_2_2:TMT134C`, `PXD053611:Fe_1st_2_2:TMT135N`, `PXD053611:Fe_phos_1_1st:TMT134C` and 47 more. Their values measure that reference, not a sample of the question. The design is copied in `sources/`, and each assay keeps its `Sample Type` (`assays.design_sample_type`). A channel marked `empty` had no sample put in it: unless the SDRF names one for it, its assay has no `sample_id`, and its values are kept as measured (isotope spill-over from a neighbouring channel, PXReprise 098), so a count of samples never counts it and a median across a run's channels must leave it out.

PTM site occupancy was not stored: this is a TMT dataset, and MetaMorpheus computes intensity occupancy for label-free searches only; its count occupancy is per file, repeated on every channel (QuantProject DEF-OCC-INT). `ptm_stoichiometry` has no rows here because of that, not because no site was modified.

No per-run `metrics` row from results.txt for `psms_1pct` (26 of 26 runs), `peptides` (26 of 26 runs), `protein_groups` (26 of 26 runs). These counts were not written, which is not a count of zero. The search task sets `WriteIndividualFiles = false`, and MetaMorpheus writes results.txt's per-file PSM, peptide and protein-group lines only when it is true (before 1.1.14, MetaMorpheus #2955, its per-file precursor and MS2 lines too). PXReprise's QC payload counts each run's share of the whole search's 1% set instead, a different number (the FDR is the whole search's, not recomputed on each file), under names of its own (`source = 'qc_payload.json'`): `psms_1pct_whole_search` for 26 of the 26 runs, `peptides_1pct_whole_search` for 26 of the 26 runs, `protein_groups_1pct_whole_search` for none of them.

dataset.summary: PXD053611 is a DDA isobaric dataset (Mus musculus) with 26 runs, 416 samples and enrichment: phospho. It was reanalysed with MetaMorpheus 1.1.14. At 1% FDR the search reports 119,179 PSMs and 3,737 protein groups; 18,751 peptidoforms pass 1% on its q-value and notch q-value, and the repository holds 40,937 PTM sites for it. 6 open warnings about it are recorded.

organisms_are: `organisms` is the organism of the protein DATABASE the search used, not a statement about the samples. Sample annotation, where any exists, is in the catalog's `samples` and `sample_characteristics` tables.
